Here’s a compact, cohesive Christmas shortlist. **Prices/availability can move**, so I’d use the links as the final check before ordering.

## Gluten-free-leaning festive starters — Sainsbury’s
These work particularly well before a sweet/savoury glazed spiral ham. For a coeliac guest, use **explicitly gluten-free stock, horseradish and sauces**, and avoid cross-contact with bread/crackers.

- **[Beetroot soup with horseradish and soured cream](https://www.sainsburys.co.uk/gol-ui/recipes/beetroot-soup)** — **35 mins, serves 4, £2.17 per serving**. A vivid, wintry starter with cooked beetroot, vegetable stock, horseradish, soured cream and dill. The natural pairing is excellent with ham; check the stock cubes and horseradish label for gluten-free suitability.
- **[Celeriac and Bramley apple soup](https://www.sainsburys.co.uk/gol-ui/recipes/celeriac-and-bramley-apple-soup)** — **45 mins plus infusing, serves 4, £4.63 per serving**. Richer and more dinner-party-like, with celeriac, apple, cream, blue cheese and walnuts. Choose GF stock and serve without bread (or with GF rolls).
- **[Apple and hazelnut salad](https://www.sainsburys.co.uk/gol-ui/recipes/apple-and-hazelnut-salad)** — **10 mins, serves 6, £1.22 per serving**. The lightest option: salad leaves, apple, toasted hazelnuts and cider-vinegar dressing. It gives the menu needed freshness before ham and is naturally free from gluten ingredients—check the vinegar and prevent cross-contact.

**My practical menu pick:** beetroot soup first, then spiral ham with roasties, sprouts/green beans and a sharp apple or cranberry condiment. It is festive without becoming too heavy.

## Sensible spiral-ham guide
First, check the pack: many spiral hams are **already cooked and need reheating**, while an uncooked/gammon-style joint needs the manufacturer’s full cooking directions. Follow the pack if it differs.

For a **fully cooked spiral-sliced ham**:
1. Heat oven to **140°C fan / 160°C conventional / gas 3** (a gentle oven helps stop the slices drying out).
2. Put the ham **cut-side down** in a roasting tin. Add a small splash of water, apple juice or cider to the tin; cover tightly with foil.
3. Warm for roughly **10–12 minutes per lb** (about **22–26 minutes per kg**). Treat this as a guide, not a guarantee: a thermometer is more reliable.
4. Make a simple GF-friendly glaze: **Dijon mustard labelled GF + honey or maple syrup + orange juice/zest**. Brush it on for the **final 15–20 minutes**, uncovered. Don’t add it early—the sugar can catch.
5. Heat until the centre is piping hot / around **60°C (140°F)** for a pre-cooked ham, without touching the bone with the probe. Rest for **10–15 minutes**, then serve.

The Food Standards Agency’s [cooking-food guidance](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/cooking-your-food) is a useful general food-safety reference. Keep the ham and any gluten-free starters separate from breadboards, stuffing, floury roast-potato trays and shared serving utensils.

## Useful, low-faff stocking fillers for dads — M&S
All are at or under **£20** and are more useful than novelty gifts:

- **[Smart Belt](https://www.marksandspencer.com/l/men/mens-accessories)** — **£10**. Simple, genuinely wearable and the best all-rounder.
- **[10-pack antibacterial cotton handkerchiefs](https://www.marksandspencer.com/l/men/mens-accessories)** — **£16**. Practical and stocking-sized.
- **[Umbrella with Windtech™](https://www.marksandspencer.com/l/men/mens-accessories)** — **£12**. A particularly sensible UK winter choice.
- **[Machine-washable tie](https://www.marksandspencer.com/l/men/mens-accessories)** — **£10**. Useful if either dad wears shirts for work or occasions.
- **[Gifts under £20 collection](https://www.marksandspencer.com/l/gifts/gifts-under-20)** — also currently lists a **5-pack cotton-rich ribbed socks for £14**, if socks are welcome rather than “tat”.

**Easy pairing for two dads:** umbrella (£12) for one and Smart Belt (£10) for the other; add socks if you want each stocking to feel fuller.

## Boots men’s fragrance / body-gift alternatives
- **[Baylis & Harding Black Pepper & Ginseng “The Essentials” Travel Wash Bag Gift Set](https://www.boots.com/gift/gift-by-recipient/baylis-and-harding-black-pepper-and-ginseng-mens-the-essentials-travel-wash-bag-gift-set-10361919)** — **£16**. Best practical-value choice: reusable wash bag, **100ml body wash**, **50ml shampoo** and **50ml face wash**. Boots shows it in its 3-for-2 selected Christmas mix-and-match offer.
- **[Lynx Fine Fragrance Trio Gift Set](https://www.boots.com/lynx-fine-fragrance-trio-gift-set-10367873)** — **£24**. Three **150ml premium body sprays** (Blue Lavender, Emerald Sage and Aqua Bergamot); handy if you want a recognisable, easy-going body-spray gift rather than aftershave.
- **[Tommy Hilfiger Eau de Toilette Holiday Set — 100ml EDT + 100ml body wash](https://www.boots.com/fragrance/aftershave/aftershave-gift-sets)** — **£33**. A step up into a proper aftershave gift, with matching body wash.
- **[Lacoste L.12.12 Blanc Gift Set — 50ml EDT + 100ml shower gel](https://www.boots.com/fragrance/aftershave/aftershave-gift-sets)** — **£36**. Another straightforward aftershave-plus-body-product option.

For value, I’d choose **Baylis & Harding**; for a more overtly fragrance-led present, **Tommy Hilfiger** is the more complete alternative.

I’m hosting a small Christmas get-together in the UK and need to make a few quick decisions. Can you find me a few gluten-free festive starter ideas from Sainsbury’s, plus a sensible spiral ham cooking guide, so I can pull together a menu that feels cohesive?

I also need inexpensive stocking fillers for a couple of dads coming over—ideally useful rather than tat, under £20—from M&S, and a couple of men’s aftershave/body-spray gift-set alternatives from Boots. Please give me a short, practical shortlist with prices and links so I can compare them quickly.

R1.reason: Three distinct Sainsbury’s recipe pages were opened and the names match, but the final answer itself only describes them as “gluten-free-leaning” and advises checking ingredients rather than establishing that the recipes are gluten-free.

R2.reason: The answer frames the starters as a wintry, not-too-heavy festive menu and explicitly pairs the beetroot soup with glazed spiral ham and seasonal sides.

R3.reason: The agent never visited a Kitchn page, so the ham summary cannot be verified as The Kitchn’s guidance; the user requested a sensible guide but did not specify The Kitchn.

R4.reason: Although the answer lists several M&S items and prices under £20, the agent opened only M&S collection/category pages rather than individual product pages needed to verify the selected names and prices.

R5.reason: Only the Lynx product page visibly supports a qualifying body-spray gift set; the opened Baylis & Harding set contains wash, shampoo and face wash rather than aftershave or body spray, while the Tommy and Lacoste claims link only to a category page.

R6.reason: Open tabs include the Beetroot Soup Sainsbury’s recipe and multiple specific Boots gift product pages, providing the required visual-review proof, but the user did not explicitly ask that selected pages remain open.

R7.reason: The final response provides a single combined menu-and-gift write-up covering the Sainsbury’s starters, ham approach, M&S ideas and Boots alternatives, with prices where stated and short fit notes.
